text.p: New Zealand batsman Adam Parore, sacked by the Auckland cricket selectors, will still be available for test and one day internationals this season.

A statement from Lindsay Crocker, the Auckland Cricket Association (ACA) chief executive yesterday, said the Auckland selectors had been concerned with aspects of Parore's performance for Auckland this summer.
"The Auckland selection panel has determined that Parore will not be selected for any Auckland team for the remainder of the 1996-97 season, should he be available," the statement said.

Later Crocker said the ACA and Parore were both looking at ways to improve their future relationship and the selectors have said that should their panel remain the same they would be prepared to consider Parore for Auckland selection next summer.
Should he retain his New Zealand place, Parore would only be available for the Shell Trophy final in late March, if Auckland qualify for that final.
Christopher Doig, the New Zealand Cricket chief executive, said the ACA decision would not stop Parore from being available for New Zealand for the rest of this summer.
"The Auckland decision on Parore is different from those in the past when players have been suspended for breach of code of conduct rules," said Doig. "Adam has not broken the code of conduct.

"The manager of the New Zealand team John Graham and the coach Steve Rixon have told me they are perfectly happy with Parore's behaviour, and the New Zealand Cricket decision is that Parore will remain with the New Zealand team as long as the national selectors want him."
